title: Resolve Review P2: add behavioral frontend and seeded UAT coverage
description: Plain-language summary: The frontend verification mostly checks source contracts and the browser smoke only proves the no-token state renders. Current behavior: Phase 1/2 are marked complete, but a seeded live workflow is still not exercised end to end. Why it matters: the accepted workflow can fail even when string checks, typecheck, lint, and build pass. Failure scenario: users cannot create a general thread, persist an answer, reload citations, or see denied patient-linked behavior despite current tests passing. Proposed fix: add behavioral frontend coverage with mocked fetch/MSW or Playwright route mocks, plus a seeded backend UAT checklist or scenario for general cited answer, patient-linked allowed answer, revoked/denied access, reload persistence, and evidence-panel fidelity. Acceptance criteria: one automated or documented seeded workflow proves create, submit, reload, citations, and denied states; current source-string checks are not the only frontend confidence path.

title: Resolve Review P2: test invalid general-answer citations
description: Plain-language summary: General-thread tests do not cover what happens when the answer generator returns no citation or an invalid citation. Current behavior: GeneralKnowledgeService raises ExternalServiceError after the user message has been flushed but before the assistant message is committed. Why it matters: the system must prove rollback or audited failure behavior so a failed generation cannot leave orphaned messages or unclear state. Failure scenario: the LLM returns text without [E1], ask_thread_message raises, and no test proves whether a partial user message was committed. Proposed fix: add a backend test that monkeypatches ChatGenerator.generate to return missing and invalid citations through ask_thread_message, then assert rollback/no orphan ChatMessage pair or a deliberate audited failure response. Acceptance criteria: invalid citation generation has deterministic tested behavior; no partial thread history is committed unintentionally; error path is safe.

title: Resolve Review P2: remove client token persistence
description: Plain-language summary: The frontend stores a bearer token in browser localStorage and can bundle a public default token through NEXT_PUBLIC_HOSPITAL_AI_DEV_TOKEN. Current behavior: AssistantShell reads and writes hospital-ai.devToken and initializes from a NEXT_PUBLIC token. Why it matters: in a PHI workflow, XSS, browser extensions, or shared machines can expose bearer tokens that can call patient-linked APIs. Failure scenario: a staff token is entered once, then later malicious client script reads localStorage and reuses the token to fetch chat threads. Proposed fix: remove NEXT_PUBLIC_HOSPITAL_AI_DEV_TOKEN and avoid localStorage token persistence; keep dev token entry memory-only or move auth to a server/session boundary with HttpOnly cookies. Acceptance criteria: no bearer token is persisted in localStorage; no public env var can ship a default bearer token to the client bundle; the no-token state remains visible.

title: Resolve Review P2: make thread-detail loading lazy and resilient
description: Plain-language summary: Opening the workspace currently fetches full details for every thread and fails the whole workspace if one detail request fails. Current behavior: AssistantShell calls getBackendChatThread for every listed thread through Promise.all. Why it matters: this couples sidebar loading to PHI-heavy transcript/evidence loading, increases latency, and discards all usable threads when one request fails. Failure scenario: one shared patient thread is revoked or temporarily errors, so the whole workspace shows a global error even though other threads were accessible. Proposed fix: load sidebar-safe summaries first, fetch selected thread details lazily, and use allSettled or per-thread error handling where bulk detail loading remains necessary. Acceptance criteria: one failed detail request does not hide other accessible threads; initial load does not pull every thread transcript/evidence before selection; UI surfaces skipped/failed thread detail counts safely.

title: Resolve Review P2: derive patient context from persisted threads
description: Plain-language summary: Patient-linked persisted threads still depend on hardcoded sample patient contexts in the frontend. Current behavior: AssistantShell sets activePatientContextId from the backend thread patient_id, but the context list comes from sampleWorkspaceState. Why it matters: a real authorized patient thread can become impossible to use when its patient_id is not one of the local samples. Failure scenario: backend returns a patient-linked thread for a real patient, the shell falls back to general context, then prepareBackendThreadMessageRequest blocks submission because the patient context does not match. Proposed fix: derive PatientContext from persisted thread/backend patient metadata or remove the local sample-context dependency for persisted thread submission and rely on the backend endpoint for permission enforcement. Acceptance criteria: real patient-linked backend threads can submit when backend permission allows; local sample contexts are not the source of truth for persisted patient IDs; denied/pending states remain visibly blocked.

title: Resolve Review P2: Add PHI boundary regression tests for permission and evidence states
description:
## Plain-Language Summary The UI shows permission states and evidence availability labels, but there are no regression tests proving blocked patient-linked evidence stays visibly blocked. For a PHI boundary, visual intent is not enough; the behavior needs executable coverage. ## What The Code Does Today - `PatientContextGate` renders general, pending, allowed, and denied permission copy from sample contexts. - `EvidencePanel` renders available, gated, unavailable, and no-evidence sample cards. - `ChatTranscript` renders citation chips whenever messages contain citations. - The diff adds typecheck/build/browser review notes, but no automated UI tests for these PHI-facing states. ## Why This Is A Problem - Decision D9 in practice: patient-linked data must be visibly permission-gated before answers or citations include it. - A future UI change can make denied/pending evidence look available or show patient-linked citation chips in the wrong context without failing tests. - This touches the same evidence boundary as prior RAG permission learnings. ## Concrete Failure Scenario - A future sample or backend-mapped message includes patient-linked citations while the active patient context is denied. - `ChatTranscript` renders citation chips because it only checks `message.citations.length`. - The screen appears to expose source evidence for denied patient context, and no automated test catches the regression. ## Evidence **File:** `app/frontend/src/components/chat/PatientContextGate.tsx` **Line(s):** 41-88 Patient scope and permission copy are UI-rendered states. **File:** `app/frontend/src/components/chat/EvidencePanel.tsx` **Line(s):** 7-35, 50-68 Evidence availability labels and styling are driven by sample state. **File:** `app/frontend/src/components/chat/ChatTranscript.tsx` **Line(s):** 45-51 ```tsx {message.citations.length > 0 ? (
{message.citations.map((citation) => ( ))}
) : null} ``` ## Known Pattern This relates to `RAG Evidence Requires Full Join-Chain Authorization`: evidence exposure has to be proved along the full path, including the UI states that make evidence appear available or blocked. ## Proposed Solutions ### Option A - Recommended: add React Testing Library coverage for PHI/evidence states **Pros:** Fast regression coverage for the exact states users see. **Cons:** Requires adding frontend test setup if the project does not already have one. **Effort:** Medium ### Option B - Add Playwright smoke coverage only **Pros:** Proves the rendered screen in a browser. **Cons:** Less precise for all state combinations unless paired with fixtures. **Effort:** Medium ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] Tests prove pending and denied patient contexts show blocked copy. - [ ] Tests prove available, no-evidence, permission-gated, and unavailable evidence labels render distinct text. - [ ] Tests prove patient-linked citation UI is not shown as available unless permission is allowed. - [ ] Tests cover empty/no-evidence and unavailable evidence states without relying on color alone.
close_reason: Completed: added PHI and evidence-state workspace regression checks

title: Resolve Review P2: Preserve backend citation evidence details for source panel
description:
## Plain-Language Summary The backend citation adapter drops the evidence fields that the source panel needs to verify an answer. It turns detailed backend citations into thin chips while the evidence panel stays bound to sample data. ## What The Code Does Today - `BackendChatCitation` includes document ID, document title, page, chunk ID, score, content, and metadata. - `mapBackendCitation` keeps only `id`, display label, evidence source ID, availability, and provenance. - `EvidencePanel` renders `sampleEvidenceSources`, not evidence generated from the active backend response. ## Why This Is A Problem - Phase 1 makes citations and source/evidence inspection first-class. - The approach explicitly says backend citation evidence fields may be rendered. - Losing document/page/chunk/score/content/metadata at the adapter boundary makes real backend wiring harder and risks a UI that looks grounded but cannot inspect the actual returned evidence. ## Concrete Failure Scenario - The backend returns three citations for a patient-scoped answer, including page, chunk ID, score, content excerpt, and metadata. - The transcript can show three citation chips. - The right evidence panel cannot show the matching excerpts or scores from that answer because the adapter discarded them and the panel still uses static sample evidence. ## Evidence **File:** `app/frontend/src/lib/chat-assistant/api.ts` **Line(s):** 16-25, 104-112 ```ts export type BackendChatCitation = { evidence_id: string; document_id: UUIDString; document_title: string; page: number; chunk_id: UUIDString; score: number; content?: string | null; metadata: Record; }; function mapBackendCitation(citation: BackendChatCitation): SourceCitation { return { id: citation.evidence_id, label: `${citation.document_title} p. ${citation.page}`, evidenceSourceId: citation.evidence_id, availability: "available", provenance: backendVerifiedProvenance, }; } ``` **File:** `app/frontend/src/components/chat/EvidencePanel.tsx` **Line(s):** 50-68 ```tsx {sampleEvidenceSources.map((item) => { ...

{item.excerpt}

... {item.score !== null ? Score {item.score.toFixed(2)} : null} ``` ## Known Pattern This matches the promoted learning `RAG Evidence Requires Full Join-Chain Authorization`: evidence/citation flows are authorization-chain problems, not just visual labels. This stays P2 because Phase 1 is UI/sample-heavy and security found no active leak, but it should be treated as known-risk work. ## Proposed Solutions ### Option A - Recommended: normalize backend citations into message plus evidence sources **Pros:** Keeps backend field names inside the adapter while preserving evidence detail for the transcript and panel. **Cons:** Requires changing adapter return shape or adding a second mapping function. **Effort:** Medium ### Option B - Extend SourceCitation with optional backend fields **Pros:** Smaller immediate patch. **Cons:** Mixes citation-chip and evidence-panel responsibilities in one type. **Effort:** Small ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] A mapped backend response can render citation chips and a matching evidence panel without `sampleEvidenceSources`. - [ ] Citation `evidenceSourceId` points to an evidence source generated from the same backend response. - [ ] Page, chunk ID, score, content, document IDs, and metadata remain available in the UI model. - [ ] Backend naming stays isolated in the adapter layer, not presentation components.
close_reason: Completed: preserved backend citation evidence details for source panel artifacts

title: Resolve Review P2: Validate patient chat request inputs before backend calls
description:
## Plain-Language Summary

The backend request helper correctly checks patient scope and permission, but it does not validate the question text or retrieval count before saying a request is ready. Invalid inputs can reach the verified patient-scoped backend path.

## What The Code Does Today

- `prepareVerifiedBackendChatRequest` rejects general scope, non-allowed permissions, and missing `patientId`.
- It returns `ready: true` with the original `question` string, including whitespace-only input.
- It accepts any `topK` value, including zero, negative values, or non-integers.

## Why This Is A Problem

- Decision D6 in practice: backend-backed fields should be used only through a real, clean contract.
- Decision D9 in practice: patient-linked requests are sensitive and should fail closed before hitting backend paths.
- Bad client-side validation creates unclear backend errors and weakens the eventual composer/API boundary.

## Concrete Failure Scenario

- A user selects an allowed patient context.
- The composer sends `question = "   "` and `topK = -1`.
- The helper marks the request ready and builds `{ patient_id, question, top_k: -1 }`.
- The backend receives an invalid request that should have been rejected before submission.

## Evidence

**File:** `app/frontend/src/lib/chat-assistant/api.ts`
**Line(s):** 46-83

```ts
export function prepareVerifiedBackendChatRequest(
  context: PatientContext,
  question: string,
  topK = 5,
): ChatSubmitReadiness {
  ...
  return {
    ready: true,
    request: {
      patient_id: context.patientId,
      question,
      top_k: topK,
    },
  };
}
```

## Proposed Solutions

### Option A - Recommended: validate and normalize in the adapter boundary
**Pros:** Keeps invalid patient-scoped requests out of the backend call path and gives the UI typed blocked reasons.
**Cons:** Requires adding readiness reasons for invalid input.
**Effort:** Small

### Option B - Validate only in composer
**Pros:** Quick UI-level fix.
**Cons:** Leaves the public helper unsafe for future callers.
**Effort:** Small

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Empty and whitespace-only questions return `ready: false` with a clear reason.
- [ ] Ready requests use the trimmed question.
- [ ] `topK` is either clamped to a safe bounded integer or rejected with a clear reason.
- [ ] Unit tests cover general scope, pending, denied, missing patient ID, invalid question, invalid `topK`, allowed request defaults/custom values, citation mapping, disclaimer preservation, and unknown confidence fallback.
close_reason: Completed: validated patient chat request inputs before backend calls

title: Resolve Review P2: Make composer submit path explicit and safe
description:
## Plain-Language Summary

The prompt composer looks like the main way to ask the assistant, but it has no controlled state or safe submit path. Users can type into it, yet send and Enter do not follow a defined chat workflow.

## What The Code Does Today

- `ChatComposer` renders a `<form>` with no `onSubmit` handler.
- The input is uncontrolled.
- The send button is `type="button"`, so clicking it does not submit the form.
- There is no disabled, loading, blocked, or error state tied to backend readiness.

## Why This Is A Problem

- Decision D2 in practice: the first screen should be a usable chat-first assistant workspace.
- Decision D5 in practice: the prompt input is part of the Phase 1 chat workspace, not decorative chrome.
- Without an explicit submit path, later backend wiring can accidentally submit unsupported general or denied patient-linked questions.

## Concrete Failure Scenario

- A reviewer types `Can I summarize this patient's latest labs?` and presses Enter.
- The UI does not append a message, show loading, validate scope, or show a blocked reason.
- A future handler might be added only to the button path and still miss keyboard submit or denied patient states.

## Evidence

**File:** `app/frontend/src/components/chat/ChatComposer.tsx`
**Line(s):** 5-30

```tsx
<form className="border-t border-white/10 bg-[#0f1011] p-3 md:p-4">
...
<input ... type="text" />
...
<Button size="icon" type="button" aria-label="Submit question">
```

## Proposed Solutions

### Option A - Recommended: controlled composer with explicit readiness
**Pros:** Makes keyboard and button submission consistent and prepares Phase 2 API wiring.
**Cons:** Requires passing active context and submit callback from the workspace state layer.
**Effort:** Medium

### Option B - Explicitly disable submission until backend wiring lands
**Pros:** Smaller patch and honest for a mock-only phase.
**Cons:** Still needs a visible blocked/local-gap state so the input does not look broken.
**Effort:** Small

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Enter key and send button follow the same submit path.
- [ ] Native form reload is prevented.
- [ ] Empty or whitespace-only questions are blocked.
- [ ] General/documented-gap and pending/denied patient states show clear blocked reasons.
- [ ] Allowed patient context creates a backend-ready request shape only after validation.
- [ ] Component or integration tests cover keyboard submit, button activation, disabled/loading state, blocked readiness reasons, success shape, and rejected submit/error state.
close_reason: Completed: made composer submit path explicit and safe

title: Resolve Review P2: Centralize chat workspace state before backend thread integration
description:
## Plain-Language Summary

The workspace looks like a shared chat app, but the selected thread and patient context are not one shared state. The sidebar can highlight one thread while the transcript and evidence panel continue reading a different sample thread.

## What The Code Does Today

- `AssistantShell` renders sidebar, patient gate, transcript, composer, and evidence panel as independent children.
- `ConversationSidebar` owns `activeThreadId` locally.
- `ChatTranscript` reads `sampleWorkspaceState.activeThreadId` directly.
- `PatientContextGate` owns its own patient context state, and `EvidencePanel` renders global sample evidence.

## Why This Is A Problem

- Decision D8 in practice: selecting a shared thread should show that conversation history, not only change sidebar highlight.
- Decision D9 in practice: patient-linked evidence needs one selected patient/context and permission state before evidence is shown.
- Fragmented state makes Phase 2 backend thread persistence harder and can mislead staff about which thread or patient context they are viewing.

## Concrete Failure Scenario

- A staff user clicks a non-active thread in the sidebar, such as a patient-context review thread.
- The sidebar row becomes active and share controls refer to that thread.
- The transcript still renders messages from the original `sampleWorkspaceState.activeThreadId`.
- The user thinks they are reading one conversation while the center panel shows another.

## Evidence

**File:** `app/frontend/src/components/chat/AssistantShell.tsx`
**Line(s):** 12-31

```tsx
<ConversationSidebar />
<PatientContextGate />
<ChatTranscript />
<ChatComposer />
<EvidencePanel />
```

**File:** `app/frontend/src/components/chat/ConversationSidebar.tsx`
**Line(s):** 10-14, 45-56

```tsx
const [activeThreadId, setActiveThreadId] = useState(sampleWorkspaceState.activeThreadId);
...
onClick={() => setActiveThreadId(thread.id)}
```

**File:** `app/frontend/src/components/chat/ChatTranscript.tsx`
**Line(s):** 6-9

```tsx
const activeThread =
  sampleWorkspaceState.threads.find((thread) => thread.id === sampleWorkspaceState.activeThreadId) ??
  sampleWorkspaceState.threads[0];
```

## Proposed Solutions

### Option A - Recommended: central workspace state hook
**Pros:** Gives the shell one source of truth and gives Phase 2 a clean adapter replacement point.
**Cons:** Requires prop wiring across current child components.
**Effort:** Medium

### Option B - Pass activeThreadId only from AssistantShell
**Pros:** Smaller immediate patch.
**Cons:** Patient context and evidence can remain fragmented unless handled soon after.
**Effort:** Small

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `AssistantShell` or a workspace hook owns active thread, active patient context, and derived evidence state.
- [ ] Selecting a sidebar thread changes the transcript content.
- [ ] Share controls, transcript, composer readiness, and evidence panel read the same active workspace model.
- [ ] Empty/no-active-thread states render without crashing.
- [ ] Add a component/integration test that fails on the current disconnected sidebar/transcript behavior and passes after the fix.
close_reason: Completed: centralized chat workspace state and added workspace wiring verification

title: Resolve Review P3: wire or remove inert sidebar controls
description: Plain-language summary: The conversation sidebar still shows dark-mode and collapse icon buttons without behavior. Current behavior: the buttons render with accessible labels but no handlers or disabled state. Why it matters: users can click controls that appear available but do nothing, which weakens trust in the live workspace. Failure scenario: a reviewer clicks collapse or dark mode expecting a Kotaemon-style control, but nothing happens and no state changes. Proposed fix: either wire real behavior for these controls or remove/disable them until implemented. Acceptance criteria: visible sidebar controls either perform a real action or are not presented as active commands.

title: Resolve Review P3: sanitize backend error display
description: Plain-language summary: The frontend can render raw backend error detail directly in the chat workspace. Current behavior: requestBackendJson includes backend message/detail text in Error.message, and AssistantShell displays that text in load/action errors. Why it matters: backend errors may contain permission details, identifiers, or internal route/debug information that should not be shown broadly in a PHI workflow. Failure scenario: a 403 or 500 response includes patient or authorization details, and the UI exposes them to the current browser session. Proposed fix: map backend errors to generic client-safe messages by status/category, and expose only a trace ID or stable error code. Acceptance criteria: UI does not render raw backend error text; detailed error content remains server-side/audit-only.

title: Resolve Review P3: move general knowledge sources behind a provider
description: Plain-language summary: The approved general knowledge catalog is hardcoded inside the answer service. Current behavior: GeneralKnowledgeService owns static policy-like sources, synthetic document IDs, ranking, and generation. Why it matters: hospital policy updates require code changes and later source management will have to unwind service-level fixture data. Failure scenario: a policy changes, but answers keep citing old hardcoded text until a developer ships a backend deploy. Proposed fix: introduce a GeneralKnowledgeRepository or retrieval provider that can later read approved non-PHI sources from the document/index store, keeping current sources as seed or test data. Acceptance criteria: answer service depends on a source provider boundary; source expansion does not require editing ranking/generation code.

title: Resolve Review P3: Consolidate duplicated chat contract and UI model types
description:
## Plain-Language Summary

The contract inventory and UI model define the same concepts twice with different names. That is manageable in a small mock, but it increases drift risk when Phase 2 connects real APIs and shared-thread persistence.

## What The Code Does Today

- `contracts.ts` defines `AssistantScope = "general" | "patient"` and `PermissionState`.
- `types.ts` defines `ChatScope = "general-knowledge" | "patient-linked"` and `PatientPermissionState`.
- Similar duplication exists around contract/data status, citations, and response shapes.

## Why This Is A Problem

- Decision D6 in practice: the frontend should clearly distinguish verified backend data from local/sample/documented gaps.
- If two type families represent the same data boundary, a future adapter can satisfy one set while bypassing the other.
- The names also differ enough that Phase 2 code may need avoidable translation between `general` and `general-knowledge`, or `patient` and `patient-linked`.

## Concrete Failure Scenario

- Phase 2 adds a general-chat adapter using `AssistantScope: "general"` because it follows `contracts.ts`.
- Existing UI readiness logic expects `ChatScope: "general-knowledge"` from `types.ts`.
- The adapter and UI gate drift, creating unnecessary conversion logic or incorrect scope handling.

## Evidence

**File:** `app/frontend/src/lib/chat-assistant/contracts.ts`
**Line(s):** 1-5, 15-39

```ts
export type ContractStatus = "verified-backend" | "local-sample-only" | "documented-gap";
export type AssistantScope = "general" | "patient";
export type PermissionState = "not-required" | "pending" | "allowed" | "denied";
```

**File:** `app/frontend/src/lib/chat-assistant/types.ts`
**Line(s):** 3-11, 43-61

```ts
export type ChatDataStatus = "verified-backend" | "local-sample-only" | "documented-gap";
export type ChatScope = "general-knowledge" | "patient-linked";
export type PatientPermissionState = "not-required" | "pending" | "allowed" | "denied";
```

## Proposed Solutions

### Option A - Recommended: make `types.ts` canonical and have contract inventory import from it
**Pros:** Keeps one source for scope, status, permission, and evidence literals.
**Cons:** Requires light refactor of contract inventory names.
**Effort:** Small

### Option B - Keep wire-format types separate only where backend names differ
**Pros:** Preserves backend/UI translation clarity.
**Cons:** Needs naming discipline to avoid semantic duplicates.
**Effort:** Small

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Scope/status/permission literals are defined once.
- [ ] Backend wire types remain separate only where field names or values actually differ.
- [ ] Contract inventory imports or references canonical UI/domain types instead of redefining equivalent literals.
- [ ] Typecheck still passes after consolidation.
close_reason: Completed: consolidated chat contract type literals
